reports.title: Peter Ross: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: has completed all the actions assigned to the department within the Trust's SI recommendations and subsequent Action Plan. If any scan is mis- reported, the Department uses it as a learning opportunity, and it is reviewed at the Departmental Radiology Event and Learning Meeting (REALM) and undertakes a process of peer review. The Radiology Department has reviewed Mr [name redacted] scans through its Governance process.
promises.summary: Radiology will review misreported scans via REALM meetings and peer review.

concerns.quote: 1.A CT C-spine requested on the admission on 8 July 2020 was misreported as normal.

2. Following that report, during the initial referral of Mr Ross to neurosurgery, the reviewing surgeon noticed an abnormality in Mr [name redacted] CT Spine, made no note of his finding and did not escalate his finding to any other clinician.
concerns.hazard: failure to document and escalate abnormal CT findings

concerns.quote: 3. Prior to burr-hole surgery, the neurosurgical team did not review the CT C spine images.
concerns.hazard: failure to review CT images before surgery

concerns.quote: 4. Repeated failures in communication between; neurosurgical, emergency medicine, nursing staff, and physiotherapists led to serious harm to Mr Ross.
5. Clinical records were poorly maintained, exacerbating the lapses in communication between those treating Mr Ross.

reports.title: George Kearsey: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: Cross site audits have been completed on COTE (Care of the Elderly) wards on a random basis to understand a cross section of compliance with fluid management with no notice given to the ward in advance of the audit. The audits capture patients who are on fluid restriction, patients requiring oral and intravenous hydration, parenteral nutrition and output monitoring, whether the intake and output is entered on Careflow Vitals and appropriate action taken as necessary. The audits were completed by
promises.summary: Cross-site audits of COTE wards to assess fluid management compliance

concerns.quote: IV fluids were not administered consistently. The longest period in which fluids were not administered was 17 hours and 45 minutes.
Contrary to Trust policy, fluid balance charts were not put in place to assess Mr [name redacted] fluid intake and output.
Clinical records were poorly maintained , resulting in an unclear picture of fluid administration.
Consultant-led ward rounds did not adequately review fluid monitoring.

reports.title: Thomas Doyle: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: An Internal Alert has been shared with staff via email, Alert reference Issued Date 9 November 2023 which details good record keeping standards that should be adhered to by all staff.
promises.summary: Share internal alert on record keeping standards

promises.quote: A video has been developed and was placed on the Trust intranet 27 November 2023 which shows - Medical Director (Patient Safety and Patient Experience), explaining the importance of good record keeping.
promises.summary: Develop and publish video on record keeping importance

promises.quote: A screen saver was agreed and appeared on all Trust computer screens week commencing 4 December 2023
promises.summary: Implement screen saver on all computers to reinforce record keeping standards

promises.quote: All medical staff must complete a record keeping module on the Trust BEST learning management system that allows staff to undertake e learning module on their first day working at the Trust.
promises.summary: Require all medical staff to complete record keeping module on first day
promises.timescale: on first day working at the Trust

promises.quote: The Trust sepsis education programme is essential for all clinical staff and has recently been updated. This is supported by additional face to face training for doctors and nurses.
promises.summary: Update sepsis education programme and provide face-to-face training

promises.quote: The Trust has adopted the UK Sepsis Trust`s adult screening tool and the use of this is audited by the Lead Nurse for Sepsis. Audits include patients who have scored over 5 on the National Early Warning Score to ensure that Sepsis was considered. In addition, all positive blood culture cases are audited to ensure compliance with the Sepsis 6.
promises.summary: Adopt UK Sepsis Trust adult screening tool and audit compliance

concerns.quote: The trust's clinical records were of a particularly poor standard which impeded the Trust's governance investigation and the inquest investigation in determining what, if any consideration was given to the possibility that Mr Doyle was suffering from an infection
The Trust's failure to commence a diagnostic pathway to investigate sepsis when clearly indicated on Mr [name redacted] admission, as required by both local policy and national guidance
concerns.hazard: failure to initiate sepsis diagnostic pathway

reports.title: David Morris: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The CQC has confirmed that they are reviewing this case, and will consider what further action should be taken, and whether any monitoring of the trust, or regulatory response, is required.
promises.summary: CQC reviewing case and considering monitoring or regulatory response

promises.quote: be able to check the wording in their specific product information to ensure the appropriate advice on checking for leaks is present.
promises.summary: Check product information for leak warnings

promises.quote: no patients that are currently on a Patient Tracker List for any cancer diagnosis can be removed or deferred without approval of the responsible consultant
promises.summary: Cancer pathway changes to prevent delays, senior oversight required

promises.quote: Critical Care Outreach Team (CCOT) model since April 2024.
promises.summary: 24/7 CCOT service for sepsis detection and escalation

promises.quote: Patient Safety Investigation Response Framework (PSIRF) which uses multidisciplinary investigations and reviews with multiple responsible authors.
promises.summary: PSIRF framework for improved incident investigation processes

concerns.quote: Mr [name redacted] diagnosis and treatment for cancer was delayed due to poor organisation and communication at the Trust.

During the evening of 3rd May 2022 going into the early hours of 4th May 2022, Doctors and nurses failed to identify the extent of Mr [name redacted] gastrostomy leak and the onset of sepsis. After identifying symptoms of sepsis, staff failed to treat and escalate Mr [name redacted] care resulting in a delay of three and a half hours before a medical review commenced emergency treatment.

During Mr [name redacted] ward-based treatment on 3 & 4th May 2022 clinical records were either of a poor standard or were non-existent. The absence of clear records impeded the effective investigation of this death by the Trust's governance teams and the Coroner.

The initial serious investigation report into Mr [name redacted] death was unfit for purpose. The report to investigate or even identify the Registrar who reviewed Mr Morris on the evening of 3rd May 2022. Since then, no effective review has been undertaken by the Trust upon how this deficient report gained executive approval.

The Trust did not have effective controlled drug management systems in place to detect a prolonged and persistent course of conduct from an employed nurse who was stealing and self- administering controlled drugs in the workplace.
concerns.hazard: lack of controlled drug management systems

reports.title: Chloe Every: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: the Trust has put mitigations in place. The Trust provides mandatory training for all staff including both nursing and medical staff related to the care of patients with a Learning Disability.
promises.summary: Mandatory training for staff on learning disability care

promises.quote: BHRUT plan to recruit more learning disability nurses in 2025. They have created pathways to encourage and upskill existing staff due to the shortage of nurses going into learning disability training (RNLD).
promises.summary: Recruit and upskill learning disability nurses by 2025

concerns.quote: The Trust does not provide nursing cover during weekends and holiday periods of staff with relevant learning disability training.
concerns.hazard: lack of nursing cover during weekends and holidays for staff with relevant learning disability training

concerns.quote: The investigation of this inquest was prejudiced by the absence of contemporary nursing and medical notes from various stages of Chloe's treatment. The extent of these lapses meant staff who made important treatment decisions could not be identified, and where staff could be identified, no contemporary account of their rationale for making treatment decisions could be located.
concerns.hazard: absence of contemporary nursing and medical notes

concerns.quote: The regularity of Chloe's clinical observations fell well below the expected level. The lapses included a period of over 10 hours in which no observations were undertaken.

Chloe underwent an enema on 8th May 2019 without informed consent being taken. The court found that Chloe was unconscious, before, during, and after the procedure, it is possible this procedure contributed to her death.
concerns.hazard: enema performed without informed consent on unconscious patient

concerns.quote: Nursing staff were incapable of explaining to the court the appropriate criteria that would have to exist before commencing CPR on an unresponsive patient.

Governance processes at the Trust failed to identify that Chloe's death constituted a patient safety incident until months after her death. A mortality review authored by the Associate Medical Director on 17th May 2019 assessed Chloe's care as good or excellent.
concerns.hazard: governance failure to identify patient safety incident
